doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Keeping recordings and programs; current work with Sebesky, Pizzarelli and Glass
summary: Raph keeps copies of meaningful recordings and programs. In 2001 he still works with Sebesky, Pizzarelli and Philip Glass but no longer does Broadway.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Do you make an effort to get copies of the recordings you play on?
Yeah. The ones that are good, I have them all. I also have all the programs of every concert that I’ve ever played from the 50s.
Wow. That’s great, you know. Most guys don’t think to do that.

No I did. I made a point out of that. There are some records that I played on that I probably don’t have but most of them I do have. The ones that were meaningful. I mean a lot of the schlock things I don’t even bother with. But these days, now I’m not going into the City on a regular basis, but what I do do still, at this point, and right now this is now November 2001, I still do pretty much all of Don Sebesky’s stuff. I do John Pizzarelli when he uses a big band, we have a couple of things coming up next month, and I do all of Phillip Glass’s work. And I’ve been doing Phillip Glass for a lot of years as I have for Sebesky. And Pizzarelli of course is a little more recent. But I have those three that I hang on to. I don’t go into town, I don’t sub shows, I should say I don’t go into town on a
regular basis. And on a regular basis means you do a Broadway show or you sub a Broadway show. I don’t do that anymore. But I do go in for dates and things.
